question:
Complete the double displacement reaction.

2NaOH + CuSO₄ → X + Na₂SO₄, here X will be ________.
solution:
The correct answer is **'__Cu(OH)2__'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, the number of Na, O, and H atoms is different in the LHS & RHS of the given equation.
 
• We need to t**ake 2 moles of ****NaOH** to balance those atoms.
 
• Hence, the balanced equation is: 
 
 
• CuSO₄ + 2NaOH ⟶ Cu(OH)₂ + Na₂SO₄
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Double Displacement reaction :**

 
• A double displacement reaction is a type of reaction where part of one reactant is replaced by part of another reactant.
 
• Double displacement reactions take the form: AB + CD → AD + CB
 
• Example: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃
